title: CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On faith: definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM SEXTUM, De fide. Atque haec de mediis salutis nostrae externis: sequitur internum, nempe FIDES, quae est assensus fiducialis atque agnitio veritatis quae est secundum pietatem, in spem vitae aeternae quam promisit qui non mentitur Deus ante tempora saecularia, et manifestavit temporibus suis (Tit. 1:1-3). Ordo postulat ut hic agamus de fide (cf. lib. IV cap.7). Hanc fidem appellat electorum, tum quia electis communis est, tum quia est de communi salute (Jude 3). Huc referri potest Apostolica descriptio Heb. 11:1: Fides est hypostasis eorum quae sperantur, elenchus rerum quae non videntur.
english: Thus far the external means of our salvation; there follows the internal, namely FAITH: a fiduciary assent and acknowledgment of the truth which is according to godliness, unto hope of eternal life which God who does not lie promised before the ages and manifested in His times (Tit. 1:1-3).
Paul calls it the faith of the elect; Hebrews 11:1 describes it as the hypostasis of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Paul calls it ye faith belonging toward ye elect; Hebrews 11:1 describes it as ye hypostasis belonging toward things hoped for, ye conviction belonging toward things not seen. — Thus far ye external means belonging toward our salvation; there follows ye internal, namely FAITH: a fiduciary assent and acknowledgment belonging toward ye truth which stands as according toward godliness, unto hope belonging toward eternal life which God who does not lie promised before ye ages and manifested in His times (Tit. 1:1-3). — CHAPTER SIXTEEN. On faith.

title: Heb. 11 terms; object of hope; things unseen
latin: Hypostasis proprie substantiam vel subsistentiam significat, quandoque audaciam et praesentiam animi. Elenchus est demonstratio, argumentum, convictio. Objectum spei tum quod speratur (vita aeterna) tum id in quod speratur (Deus, Christus). Non solum futura bona, verum etiam praesentia et praeterita quae credimus facta et confidimus mansura pertinent. Addit Apostolus ea quae non videntur—multa eius conditionis ut fide apprehendantur.
english: Hypostasis properly means substance or subsistence, sometimes boldness of soul. Elenchus is demonstration and conviction.

Hope's object is both what is hoped for (eternal life) and that in which one hopes (God, Christ). Present and past goods believed done and trusted to remain also belong here, with things unseen that faith must apprehend.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Hope's object stands as both what stands as hoped for (eternal life) and that in which one hopes (God, Christ). Present and past goods believed done and trusted toward remain also belong here, with things unseen that faith must apprehend. — Hypostasis properly means substance or subsistence, sometimes boldness belonging toward soul. Elenchus stands as demonstration and conviction.

title: Kinds and grades of faith
latin: Distinguenda est fides historica, dogmatica, temporalis, miraculosa, et fides iustificans seu salvifica. Fides historica est notitia et assensus historiae Evangelicae sine fiducia. Temporalis germinat in petrosis et aestu persecutionis arescit. Miraculosa credit potentiae divinae ad mira. Fides iustificans sola salvat: notitia, assensus, fiducia in Christum mediatorem, apprehendens promissionem Euangelii ad iustificationem et vitam aeternam.
english: Faith is distinguished as historical, dogmatic, temporary, miraculous, and justifying or saving faith.

Historical faith knows and assents to Gospel history without trust; temporary faith sprouts on rocky ground and withers under persecution; miraculous faith credits divine power for wonders. Justifying faith alone saves: knowledge, assent, and trust in Christ the mediator, apprehending the Gospel promise unto justification and eternal life.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Historical faith knows and assents toward Gospel history without trust; temporary faith sprouts on rocky ground and withers under persecution; miraculous faith credits divine power for wonders. Justifying faith alone saves: knowledge, assent, and trust in Christ ye mediator, apprehending ye Gospel promise unto justification and eternal life. — Faith stands as distinguished as historical, dogmatic, temporary, miraculous, and justifying or saving faith.

title: Justifying faith: knowledge, assent, trust; instrument
latin: In fide iustificante concurrunt notitia veritatis Euangelicae, assensus firmus, et fiducia qua peccator in solum Christum pro remissione peccatorum et acceptatione apud Deum recumbit. Fides est organon sive instrumentum iustificationis, non causa meritoria; Christus et eius iustitia sunt obiectum et fundamentum. Fides apprehendit, non meretur.
english: In justifying faith concur knowledge of Gospel truth, firm assent, and the trust by which the sinner rests on Christ alone for remission of sins and acceptance with God.
Faith is the organ or instrument of justification, not a meritorious cause; Christ and His righteousness are the object and foundation. Faith apprehends; it does not earn.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Faith stands as ye organ or instrument belonging toward justification, not a meritorious cause; Christ and His righteousness stand as ye object and foundation. Faith apprehends; it does not earn. — In justifying faith concur knowledge belonging toward Gospel truth, firm assent, and ye trust by which ye sinner rests on Christ alone for remission belonging toward sins and acceptance with God.

title: Faith's effects toward Cap.17; against idle faith
latin: Fides viva non est otiosa sed per charitatem efficax (Gal. 5:6); tamen iustificat sola, non quatenus operatur, sed quatenus Christum apprehendit. Effecta fidei—unio cum Deo, iustificatio Euangelica, sanctificatio, pax conscientiae—sequenti capite tractantur. CAPUT DECIMUM SEPTIMUM sequitur, De fidei Christianae consequentibus et effectis.
english: Living faith is not idle but effective through love (Gal. 5:6); yet it justifies alone—not insofar as it works, but insofar as it apprehends Christ.
Faith's effects—union with God, evangelical justification, sanctification, peace of conscience—are treated in the next chapter.
CHAPTER SEVENTEEN follows, On the consequences and effects of Christian faith.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER SEVENTEEN follows, On ye consequences and effects belonging toward Christian faith. — Faith's effects—union with God, evangelical justification, sanctification, peace belonging toward conscience—are treated in ye next chapter. — Living faith stands as not idle but effective through love (Gal. 5:6); yet it justifies alone—not insofar as it works, but insofar as it apprehends Christ.
